html:
The Luckiamute were a band of the Kalapuya people of the Willamette Valley in Oregon, living along the Luckiamute River west of present Albany.

Like other Kalapuya, they gathered camas roots and acorns and burned the valley grasslands to keep them open for game. Malaria and other epidemics in the 1830s killed most of the valley's people. As settlers arrived along the Oregon Trail, the survivors signed the Willamette Valley Treaty of 1855 and were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation. Their kin included the Santiam and Yamhill. See also Grand Ronde.
sum: The Luckiamute were a band of the Kalapuya people of the Willamette Valley in Oregon, living along the Luckiamute River west of present Albany.
